review_notes: I read the whole file and the sibling files First.lean, DividedSquare.lean, Exponential.lean, Modular/Matrix.lean, Modular/DividedAction.lean, Modular/Action.lean, and Tits/Basic.lean and ReeF4/Basic.lean. I checked which simp lemmas fire on the column definitions and on isogenyReverse/isogenyExponent. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour that I observed. Downstream proofs mostly use `simp only` or `rw`. Changing the global simp set could therefore affect call sites that rely on the first column staying in the form `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint k (basis a)`. I did not report the other unfolding simp lemmas (`f4ShortRootQuotientFirstColumn_eq` and similar), since they are used as explicit unfold rules and chain consistently with the other simp lemmas.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_apply
    (k : Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4) (a : Fin 26) :
    f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn k a =
      f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint k (f4ShortRootLieIdealBasis a) := by
findings.problem: The simp interface for the ideal-side columns is asymmetric. For the divided-square column, the simp unfolding lemma `f4ShortRootIdealDividedSquareColumn_apply` sends the column to `f4ShortRootDividedAdjointSquare k (basis a)`. The simp lemma `f4ShortRootDividedAdjointSquare_basis` then rewrites that to the sparse form `coeff • basis target`. For the first-order column, the simp lemma `f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_apply` also unfolds it, to `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint k (basis a)`. The sparse-form lemma for that expression is the private theorem `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint_basis` in Modular/Matrix.lean, which is not simp. The public sparse-form lemma `f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_eq` is not simp either. So simp on a first column stops at the intermediate adjoint form, while the divided-square column goes all the way to the sparse normal form. A user has to rewrite by hand with `f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_eq`, and that rewrite is not applied by simp once `_apply` has already unfolded the column.
findings.proposed_change: Make the two columns behave the same way. Preferred option: add a public simp lemma `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint k (f4ShortRootLieIdealBasis a) = (f4SimpleRootCoeff k a : ZMod 2) • f4ShortRootLieIdealBasis (f4SimpleRootTarget k a)`, either by making the Modular/Matrix.lean lemma public and `@[simp]` or by restating it. This mirrors `f4ShortRootDividedAdjointSquare_basis`. Alternative: stop using `_apply` as a global simp lemma, and mark `f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_eq` as the canonical `@[simp]` rewrite for the column. Downstream `simp only [f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_apply]` calls (DividedSquare.lean lines 338, 412, 545) would need checking against whichever option is chosen.
findings.benefit: `simp` normalises both kinds of ideal columns to the same sparse `coeff • basis target` form. Proofs about first-order columns no longer need a manual rewrite with `f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_eq`, and the simp set no longer leaves a half-unfolded `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint k (basis a)` term.

findings.excerpt:
@[expose] def isogenyReverse : Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4 → Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4 :=
  Sum.map Fin.revPerm Fin.revPerm
findings.problem: The only simp lemma for these data definitions is the involution `isogenyReverse_isogenyReverse`. There are no evaluation lemmas on `Sum.inl`/`Sum.inr`, such as `isogenyReverse (.inl i) = .inl i.rev` or `isogenyExponent (.inl i) = ![1,1,2,2] i`. Every user must unfold the definition by name and add `Sum.map_inl`/`Sum.map_inr`. This happens at lines 246, 255 and 271 of this file, in First.lean (lines 178, 183, 194, 201), and in Tits/Basic.lean line 81 and ReeF4/Basic.lean line 75. Tits/Basic.lean line 67 also re-proves a per-index `isogenyExponent (.inl j)` formula with `decide`. Unfolding the definition inside a bare `simp` is not an ideal normal form either, because it exposes `Sum.map Fin.revPerm Fin.revPerm`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` evaluation lemmas `isogenyReverse_inl : isogenyReverse (Sum.inl i) = Sum.inl (Fin.rev i)`, `isogenyReverse_inr`, and `isogenyExponent_inl`/`isogenyExponent_inr` (the latter stated as `![1,1,2,2] i`). Their proofs would be `rfl`. Then replace the `simp only [isogenyReverse, Sum.map_inl, ...]` calls with these lemmas, so the definition itself stays folded.
findings.benefit: Simp normalises these terms uniformly and the call sites stop repeating the unfolding recipe. It also keeps `isogenyReverse k` for a variable `k` folded, so `isogenyReverse_isogenyReverse` stays applicable.
